# Depth and Geometry Supervision

Also called: Depth-supervised NeRF, Guided Optimization, Single-view Depth NeRF

## Overview
Depth and Geometry Supervision refers to a family of NeRF training procedures that incorporate external geometric priors—such as monocular depth estimates, sparse 3D keypoints, or multi-view consistency errors—to regularize the density field $\sigma$ and mitigate the shape-radiance ambiguity inherent in inverse volume rendering [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md][7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md][8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md]. Unlike standard NeRF, which relies solely on RGB reconstruction loss, these methods enforce geometric constraints by either guiding the spatial distribution of samples along rays or by imposing explicit losses on rendered depth distributions, thereby accelerating convergence and improving quality in sparse-view or single-view settings [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md][7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family integrate geometric information into the NeRF optimization loop to constrain the density field $\sigma$. The core mechanism involves modifying the standard volume rendering pipeline to account for depth. This is achieved through one of two primary strategies:
1.  **Guided Sampling:** The sampling intervals $[t_n, t_f]$ along camera rays are adapted based on external depth priors, restricting the search space for geometry [7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md].
2.  **Explicit Depth Loss:** A loss term is added to the optimization objective that compares rendered depth (derived from the ray termination distribution $h(t) = T(t)\sigma(t)$) against a supervision distribution derived from geometric priors [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md].

In all cases, the NeRF network $F_\theta: (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (c, \sigma)$ is optimized to minimize a combined loss including the standard RGB reconstruction error and a geometry-aware term [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md][7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md][8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md].

## Subtopics

### [Guided Optimization of NeRF](7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md)
Mitigates shape-radiance ambiguity in indoor scenes by using adapted monocular depth priors and multi-view consistency errors to define adaptive sampling ranges $[t_n, t_f]$ centered on the estimated depth. It differs from explicit loss methods by constraining *where* samples are drawn rather than penalizing depth errors directly, and it refines depth maps using confidence scores derived from RGB reconstruction errors. Choose this when multi-view consistency is available and adaptive sampling is preferred over explicit depth losses.

### [Single-view NeRF Training with Depth Map](8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md)
Addresses the under-constrained problem of 360-degree reconstruction from a single panorama by initializing geometry via deformable alignment of multiple perspective depth projections to a canonical panorama depth map. Unlike [Depth-Supervised NeRF](8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md), it explicitly constructs a consistent depth map before training to resolve scale ambiguity, rather than applying depth loss directly to rendered depths during standard optimization. Choose this for single-view panoramic scenes where scale consistency is critical.

### [Depth-Supervised NeRF](8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md)
Accelerates optimization in sparse-view settings by incorporating depth supervision from sparse 3D keypoints generated during Structure-from-Motion (SfM) preprocessing. It imposes a loss that forces the rendered ray termination distribution to match the surface priors given by these keypoints, effectively regularizing $\sigma$ without requiring additional training data or domain-specific assumptions. Choose this when sparse SfM keypoints are available and explicit depth supervision is desired.

## Background
The concept of using depth supervision to regularize NeRFs was introduced to address the ill-posed nature of inverse volume rendering, particularly in sparse-view scenarios where RGB loss alone leads to ambiguous geometries [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. The foundational work, Depth-Supervised NeRF (DS-NeRF), utilized sparse 3D keypoints from SfM to provide geometric constraints [8687-depth-supervised-nerf.md]. Subsequent works extended this to monocular depth priors for guided sampling [7496-guided-optimization-of-nerf.md] and single-view panorama reconstruction via deformable alignment [8679-single-view-nerf-training-with-depth-map.md]. These methods collectively establish depth and geometry supervision as a standard technique for improving NeRF robustness and convergence.
